title: Free to apply isn’t always free: the fees an open call can charge
seoTitle: Art Competition Entry Fees, Hanging and Participation Fees
description: Entry, jury, hanging and participation fees and sales commission explained: when you pay each one, what’s fair, and how to find every cost before you apply.
summary: Entry, hanging and participation fees and sales commission: when each one is charged, and how to find the full cost before you apply.
secondaryKeywords: are art competition fees worth it
answer: An entry fee pays for your work to be considered. A hanging fee pays to show selected work. A participation fee covers taking part once you’re selected. A call can charge none, one or several of these, plus commission on sales. Before you apply, find what it costs to enter and what you’d owe if accepted.
keyPoints: Entry and jury fees pay for consideration, not a place in the show.
Free to enter can still mean a participation fee, shipping and framing once you’re selected.
Budget for two outcomes before you pay: rejected and accepted, with no sale assumed.
illustrationAlt: Illustration separating an entry fee, a participation fee and sales commission.
